Question 35

You want to calculate the proportion who voted separately for each education category in survey. The variable voted is coded 1 = voted and 0 = did not vote, with no missing values. A classmate suggests first using summarize(Turnout = mean(voted)) and then using group_by(Education). What is the problem with this order?

A. mean() cannot be used with a variable coded 0 and 1.

B. Summarizing the ungrouped data first produces one overall turnout proportion and drops Education; use group_by(Education) before summarize() to calculate turnout separately for each category.

C. group_by() must come after summarize() but before mean().

D. There is no problem: grouping afterward divides the overall proportion into the correct category proportions.

Assume values are nonnegative and there are no missing values. Which statement best explains when to use if_else() versus case_when()?

A. if_else() is for numerical outcomes only, while case_when() is for text outcomes only.

B. case_when() is required whenever a variable has more than two observations.

C. if_else() changes existing columns, while case_when() can only create new columns.

D. if_else() is convenient for the two outcomes in the first variable; case_when() is convenient for expressing the multiple conditions in the second variable without nesting if_else() calls.

This exercise is worth 5 points. Consider the code chunk below and answer all four parts:

2a. In the code chunk below, comment on what each line does.

library(tidyverse)

dat = readRDS(file="MyData.rds")

dat = dat |>
  filter(college == "Vanderbilt" & class == "PSCI 2300") |>
  select(c(PS1,PS2,PS3)) |>
  summarize(Blah1 = mean(PS1,na.rm=TRUE),
            Blah2 = mean(PS2,na.rm=TRUE),
            Blah3 = mean(PS3,na.rm=TRUE)) |>
  mutate(Goo = (Blah1 + Blah2 + Blah3)/3,
         Moo = Goo)

Exercise 3: Reminder texts and turnout

This exercise is worth 5 points. Answer all eight parts.

A campaign sent reminder texts to some registered voters. The dataset reminder has 600 voters and no missing values. texted equals 1 if the voter received a text and 0 otherwise. voted equals 1 if the voter turned out and 0 otherwise. Of the 200 voters who were texted, 150 voted. Of the 400 voters who were not texted, 200 voted. The campaign texted voters who had voted in the previous election.

For parts after 3b, assume XX and YY have been correctly filled in to calculate texted minus not texted.

reminder |>
  group_by(texted) |>
  summarize(N = n(),
            Turnout = mean(voted))

A = reminder |>
  filter(texted == 1) |>
  summarize(Turnout = mean(voted))

B = reminder |>
  filter(texted == 0) |>
  summarize(Turnout = mean(voted))

Gap = XX - YY
set.seed(42)
SampledGaps = NULL

for (i in 1:1000) {
  one_sample = reminder |>
    slice_sample(prop = 1, replace = TRUE)

  one_texted = one_sample |>
    filter(texted == 1) |>
    summarize(Turnout = mean(voted))

  one_not = one_sample |>
    filter(texted == 0) |>
    summarize(Turnout = mean(voted))

  one_gap = tibble(Gap = one_texted$Turnout - one_not$Turnout)

  SampledGaps = bind_rows(SampledGaps, one_gap)
}

SampledGaps |>
  summarize(Lower = quantile(Gap, p = .025),
            Upper = quantile(Gap, p = .975))

After filling in XX and YY, the last block gives the following interval (rounded to three decimal places):
